page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The three colours
lines: The heat of the flame lifts the outer
electrons to a higher energy level, and
light of a definite colour is given out
Calcium gives a brick red flame.
Strontium gives a crimson red flame.
Barium gives an apple green flame.
steps.why: The colour comes from the energy gap the excited electron falls back through, and each metal has its own gap, so the flame colour identifies the metal.
common_mistakes: Swapping strontium and barium. Strontium gives crimson red and barium gives apple green.
Giving one colour for the whole group. Each metal has its own colour.
steps.memory_tip: Calcium brick red, strontium crimson red, barium apple green.
steps.margin_note: Write the metal beside each colour.

steps.label: Beryllium and magnesium
lines: Beryllium and magnesium give no colour
Their electrons are too strongly bound
to be excited by the heat of a bunsen
flame, so no visible light is given out.
in group 2, are a measure of that strong
steps.why: A flame test works only when the flame is hot enough to excite the outer electrons. In beryllium and magnesium those electrons are bound too strongly for a bunsen flame to excite, so for them the answer is the absence of a colour. The excitation energy is the quantity that matters here; the ionisation enthalpy is a separate quantity and is quoted only as evidence of how tightly the electrons are bound.
common_mistakes: Giving beryllium or magnesium a colour. Neither of them colours a bunsen flame.
Writing that they have low ionisation enthalpies. Theirs are the highest in group 2, and their electrons are correspondingly hard to excite in a bunsen flame.
steps.memory_tip: The two smallest metals of the group, beryllium and magnesium, give no flame colour.
steps.margin_note: State plainly that beryllium and magnesium give no colour, and give the reason.

insider_note: A complete answer names the three coloured metals with their colours and says that beryllium and magnesium give no flame colour at all.
